question.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$U=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ 4 & -3\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $U-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
U-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 5 \\ 4 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(U-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(U-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 5 \\ 4 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-2-\lambda )(-3-\lambda )-5\cdot 4 & =0 \\ 6+2\lambda +3\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-20 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+5\lambda -14 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{-5\pm \sqrt{{5}^{2}+4\cdot 1\cdot 14}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-5\pm \sqrt{81}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-5\pm 9}{2} \\  & =-7,2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =-7$ and $\lambda =2.$
